summary: Guidance for isolating bursty short-HTTP traffic from long-lived worker heartbeats to prevent tenant 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports repeated 429s affecting low-latency storefront chat endpoints after they recently increased parallel short HTTP requests from web clients. Simultaneously they run long-lived background workers that send heartbeat/telemetry pings every 10s. The customer suspects tenant quota bleed between the two flows and asks for an operational plan to separate bursty user requests from background work so interactive traffic does not hit tenant-level 429s.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s on /v1/chat/stream and /v1/generate during peak minutes (09:00-10:30 PDT).
- Checkout chat widget times out for ~3-5% of sessions, increasing perceived latency and abandoned carts.
- Customer on Dedicated pool; wants configuration guidance rather than aggressive changes to code.

Traffic profile (provided by customer):
- 600-900 short HTTP POSTs/min to chat endpoints during peak, average payload 1.2k tokens. Many originate from mobile clients with flaky networks causing retries.
- 120 background worker connections per minute that emit 1 small telemetry call (50-120 bytes) and a heartbeat call every 10s.

Steps to reproduce (customer environment):
1) Run background workers (N=120) configured to send heartbeat every 10s to /internal/ping.
2) Simulate 700 concurrent short POSTs to /v1/chat/stream over 12 minutes with exponential backoff retries on 5xx/429.
3) Observe increased 429 rate on chat endpoints; logs show intermittent 429s attributed to tenant token bucket exhaustion.

Recent changes:
- On 2026-03-08 BrightCart switched from multiplexed HTTP/2 connections to many short-lived HTTP/1.1 POSTs to mitigate a client-side proxy bug.
- No model version change.

Temporary mitigation requested:
- Configuration that avoids broad tenant-level throttling while preserving background worker telemetry. Customer asks for recommended rate-limiter split and concrete console steps they can apply safely.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 - Support (Asha): Received logs and traffic profile. Asked for example client request timing and whether background pings are authenticated with the same API key. Requested a short HAR and list of endpoints.

2026-03-10 10:12 - Customer (BrightCart - Lina Chen): Confirmed both user chat and worker heartbeats use the same service API key and originate from the same CIDR set. Provided sample request headers and a 10-minute span of edge metrics (429 spikes at 09:05 and 09:22).

2026-03-11 11:00 - SRE (Marcus): Hypothesis: token-bucket accounting counts all requests under the tenant pool; frequent small heartbeat calls plus short-lived connection retries spike the refill window exhaustion. Will run burst isolation test in staging: create a priority-based split (priority=high for chat routes, low for heartbeat) and apply a dedicated small burst pool for the heartbeats.

2026-03-11 16:30 - Engineering (Marcus): Deployed non-production patch to rate-limiter to allow per-route burst pools for this customer. Observed staging: chat 429s dropped from 2.8% -> 0.2% under identical synthetic load. Noted edge case: HTTP/1.1 connection churn increases preflight counting; recommend keepalive and connection pooling on client if possible.

2026-03-12 08:10 - Support (Asha): Shared recommended config and console steps with customer and scheduled a short maintenance window to apply to prod during off-peak (2026-03-13 01:00-02:00 PDT). Asked customer to enable connection pooling in the short-term.
2026-03-12 09:02 - Customer (Lina): Accepts maintenance window and will coordinate with platform ops. Will also roll a small client fix to add TLS keepalive settings.
investigation_notes: Edge metrics: token_bucket.available dropped to zero at the tenant level during mini-bursts (90s windows) — correlates to peak times in customer data.
Heartbeat calls are small but frequent; under tenant-level token accounting they aggregated to ~18% of tokens during peak due to high frequency and retry amplification from flaky mobile clients.

HTTP/1.1 short-lived connections caused additional preflight/accounting noise vs HTTP/2 multiplexing; confirmed by comparing staging traces (multiplexed flow had ~12% fewer counted requests in same workload).
Rate-limiter supports route-level buckets and priority lanes; customer's Dedicated pool currently only uses tenant-level pooled budgeting without separation.
suggested_config: 1) Create two route-level buckets: 'interactive:chat' with high-priority lane and 'background:heartbeat' with low-priority small burst pool.
2) Example values to start (prod): interactive:chat -> refill: 1200 tokens/min, burst: 800 tokens; background:heartbeat -> refill: 200 tokens/min, burst: 100 tokens.
3) Set priority weight: interactive=100, background=10 so background yields when tenant pressure occurs.
4) On Dedicated console: create per-route policy and bind to route patterns /v1/chat/* (interactive) and /internal/ping (background); enable "isolate_burst_pool" flag.
5) Encourage client-side keepalive/connection pooling to reduce preflight counting; if not possible, increase background route's smoothing interval to 20s to reduce refill pressure.
6) Monitoring: create dashboard with per-route token consumption, refill exhaustion events, and 429 counts; set alert if chat 429s > 0.5% for 15m.
next_steps: Apply per-route burst pool policy in prod during agreed maintenance window (2026-03-13 01:00-02:00 PDT).
Post-change: run synthetic peak test and compare 429 and token_bucket.available metrics.
If improvement < 80% reduction in chat 429s, increase interactive burst pool by +25% and further smooth background refill interval.
Document permanent config in Confluence and propose a Dedicated best-practice for separating telemetry/background flows from user-facing routes.
Customer to add connection pooling change in client and report results within 48h after deployment.
resolution: Ongoing - per-route burst pools implemented in staging with positive results; prod change scheduled for 2026-03-13. Waiting on post-deploy metrics and customer client keepalive rollout.
workaround: Recommend immediate client-side mitigation: enable persistent connections / keepalive and add jittered retry backoff (base 250ms, max 2000ms) to reduce synchronized retry waves.
follow_up_actions: SRE to run post-deploy load test and upload results to ticket (expected by 2026-03-13 04:00 PDT).
Support to create a compact KB article showing console steps to configure per-route burst pools for Dedicated tenants.
Engineering to evaluate automating a suggested split for Dedicated onboarding when workload telemetry shows >10% small high-frequency calls.
